title: The Night Watchman's Secret
summary: Two curious children discover that their building's night watchman tends a hidden garden to quietly grow vegetables for elderly neighbors who cannot easily shop for themselves.
poll: A small, quiet act of kindness matters just as much as a big, public one.

versions.title: The Night Watchman's Secret
versions.text:
Saleh is a watchman. He works at night. He keeps a place safe. He is kind. He likes his job.

Yousef and Mira live there too. Each night, they look out. They see Saleh. He goes out back. He has a small garden.

Saleh waters his plants. He pulls weeds. He does this each night. He does not stop. He does not rest.

Yousef and Mira want to know. Is it a secret? They do not know yet. They want to ask him.

One night, they ask him. "What do you grow?" says Yousef.

Saleh smiles. "Vegetables," he says. "Tomatoes and mint."

"Who eats them?" asks Mira.

Saleh says, "I give them to the elderly. They cannot walk to the shop."

It is not a secret. It is just kind. Saleh likes to help. He asks for no thanks.

Yousef and Mira smile. The next night, they help too.

Saleh works as the watchman for a tall place in the city. He watches over it and keeps it safe while people sleep. He likes his job.

Yousef and his younger sister, Mira, live in that same place. Each night, they look out. They see Saleh walk to the back. There is a small, hidden garden there.

Saleh waters the plants with care. He pulls out the weeds too. He does this every night. He does not stop, even when he is tired.

Yousef and Mira want to know about this. Could Saleh be hiding a secret back there? They want to find out the truth.

One evening, the two children walk over. "What do you grow back here every night?" Yousef asks.

Saleh smiles and wipes the soil from his hands. He explains, "I grow vegetables. Tomatoes, mint, and a few cucumbers."

Mira asks, "But who eats all of them?" She looks at the neat rows of plants.

Saleh says softly, "I give most of them to the elderly who live here. They cannot walk to the shop easily anymore."

It is not a scary secret. It is simply a kind, quiet thing that Saleh does every night. He asks for no thanks.

Yousef and Mira smile at each other. The next evening, they come back to help Saleh water his garden.

versions.title: The Night Watchman's Secret
versions.text:
A man named Saleh works as the watchman for a tall building in the city. He watches over the building and keeps everyone safe while they sleep.

Yousef and his younger sister, Mira, live in that same building. Each night before bed, they look out their window. They see Saleh walk quietly to the back. There is a small, hidden garden there.

Saleh waters the plants there with care. He pulls out weeds and checks each one closely. He does this every single night, no matter how tired he looks after his shift.

Yousef and Mira grow more curious about this habit. Could Saleh be hiding a secret back there? They want to find out what is going on.

One evening, the two children walk over. They quietly ask him about it. "What do you grow back here every night?" Yousef asks.

Saleh smiles kindly and wipes the soil from his hands. He explains, "I grow vegetables. Tomatoes, mint, and a few cucumbers, mostly."

Mira asks, "But who eats all of them?" She looks at the neat rows of plants along the wall.

Saleh says softly, "I give most of them to the elderly who live in this building. Many of them cannot walk to the shop easily, so I like to help however I can."

Yousef asks, "Why didn't you ever tell anyone?"

Saleh shrugs. He says, "It never felt like something that needed telling. It is simply a kind, quiet thing that I enjoy doing every night."

Yousef and Mira smile at each other. The next evening, they come back to help Saleh water his little garden.

versions.title: The Night Watchman's Secret
versions.text:
A man named Saleh worked as the watchman for a tall building in the city. He kept watch over the building and made sure everyone inside stayed safe while they slept.

Yousef and his younger sister, Mira, lived in that building. Each night, they liked to look out their window. They always noticed Saleh walking quietly to the back, where a small, hidden garden grew along the wall.

Saleh would tend to the plants there with care, pulling weeds and checking each row, night after night, no matter how tired he felt.

Before long, Yousef and Mira grew very curious about this strange habit. Was their watchman hiding some sort of secret back there in the dark? They decided they had to find out.

One evening, the two children finally walked over to ask him. "What exactly do you grow back here every night?" Yousef asked.

Saleh smiled and wiped the soil from his hands. "Vegetables," he explained. "Tomatoes, mint, and a few cucumbers, mostly."

"But who eats all of them?" Mira asked, studying the neat rows of plants.

"I give most of it to the elderly neighbors who live in this building," Saleh said gently. "Many of them can no longer walk to the market easily, so this is simply my small way of helping out."

"Why did you never mention it to anyone?" Yousef asked.

Saleh only shrugged. "It never felt like something that needed announcing," he said. "A little kindness doesn't have to be loud to matter."

Deeply impressed by his quiet, generous habit, Yousef and Mira smiled at each other. The next evening, both children came back to help their watchman water his small garden.

versions.title: The Night Watchman's Secret
versions.text:
A man named Saleh worked as the watchman for a tall apartment building in a busy, crowded part of the city. He kept diligent watch over the entire building, making sure everyone inside stayed safe while they slept soundly through the long, quiet night.

Yousef and his younger sister, Mira, lived in that same building. Each evening before bed, they liked to look out their window, and they consistently noticed Saleh walking quietly toward the back of the building, where a small, hidden garden grew along the rear wall, largely unnoticed by the building's other, preoccupied residents.

Saleh tended the plants there with evident, careful attention, pulling weeds and inspecting each row closely, night after night, regardless of how exhausted he felt after his long evening shift.

Before long, Yousef and Mira grew intensely curious about this peculiar nightly habit. Could their building's unassuming watchman possibly be concealing some sort of secret back there in the darkness? They resolved that they absolutely had to discover what was actually happening, however long it might take.

One evening, the two children finally summoned their courage and approached him directly. "What exactly do you grow back here every single night?" Yousef inquired.

Saleh smiled warmly and wiped the dark soil from his weathered hands. "Vegetables," he explained patiently. "Tomatoes, mint, and a handful of cucumbers, mostly, depending entirely on the season."

"But who actually eats all of them?" Mira asked, studying the neat, orderly rows of plants stretching along the wall.

"I provide most of these provisions to the elderly neighbors living in this building," Saleh said gently. "Umm Fahd on the second floor, for instance, can no longer walk to the market easily, so this remains simply my modest way of helping quietly, without any fuss."

"Why did you never acknowledge any of this to anyone before now?" Yousef asked.

Saleh merely shrugged, humble as ever. "It never felt like something requiring announcement," he said. "A considerate act of kindness doesn't need to be loud or publicly celebrated in order to genuinely matter."

Deeply moved by his quiet, compassionate habit, Yousef and Mira exchanged warm, knowing smiles. The very next evening, both children returned eagerly to help their watchman water his small, well-tended garden, and the three of them soon developed a cherished nightly routine.

Yousef and his younger sister, Mira, lived in that same building. Saleh tended the plants there with evident, meticulous attention, pulling weeds and inspecting each row closely, night after night, regardless of how exhausted he felt following his long and often demanding evening shift.

Before long, Yousef and Mira grew intensely curious about this peculiar nightly habit. Could their building's unassuming watchman possibly be concealing some sort of secret back there in the darkness? They resolved that they absolutely had to discover what was actually taking place, however long it might take them.

One evening, the two children finally summoned their courage and approached him directly. "What exactly do you grow back here every single night?" Yousef inquired, genuinely curious.

Saleh smiled warmly and wiped the dark soil from his weathered, calloused hands. "Vegetables," he explained patiently. "Tomatoes, mint, and a handful of cucumbers, mostly, depending entirely on the season and the rainfall."

"But who actually eats all of them?" Mira asked, studying the neat, orderly rows of plants stretching along the wall with evident admiration.

"I provide most of these provisions to the elderly neighbors living in this building," Saleh said gently. "Umm Fahd on the second floor, for instance, can no longer walk to the market easily, so this remains simply my modest way of helping quietly, without any fuss or expectation of thanks."

"Why did you never acknowledge any of this to anyone before now?" Yousef asked, still puzzled.

Saleh merely shrugged, humble as always, and smiled faintly. "It never felt like something requiring announcement," he said. "A considerate act of kindness doesn't need to be loud or publicly celebrated in order to genuinely matter to the person receiving it."

Deeply moved by his quiet, compassionate habit, Yousef and Mira exchanged warm, knowing smiles. The very next evening, both children returned eagerly to help their watchman water his small, well-tended garden, and the three of them soon developed a cherished nightly routine that continued happily for months.

MID.modelAnswer: Saleh never told anyone about his garden because he did not think a kind act needed to be announced. HIGH.prompt: The story ends by calling Saleh's garden 'a lesson in... everyday generosity.' Do you agree that small, quiet acts of kindness matter as much as big ones? Support your answer with evidence from the story.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the question.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that small, quiet acts of kindness matter as much as big, public ones. Saleh spent nearly ten years tending his garden simply to provide vegetables for elderly neighbors like Umm Fahd, without ever telling anyone or expecting thanks. His habit made a real difference to people who could not easily walk to the market, even though no one praised him for it. Someone might argue that a larger, public act of charity would help more people at once, but Saleh's story shows that consistent, unnoticed kindness, repeated night after night for years, can quietly support a whole community just as effectively.
